column1: # 7장 말투 지시(11-10). 열: 조각 앞머리 → 지시(영어, 짧게). @scene 행은 장면 설명(장면 끝까지 모든 요청에 붙는다).

column2: Monday morning. Marc, the reserved locksmith, picks Yuna up on an old sky-blue Vespa to go to the city archive and look for the vanished street. He asks if she has had breakfast with the present perfect, "¿Has desayunado?", and Yuna answers with the new form, "He desayunado". Dry, companionable, few words.
careful, using a new verb form; stress "He desayunado"

In the Gothic Quarter, Marc shows Yuna the cathedral and a marble letterbox carved with swallows and a turtle. With a straight face he jokes that the swallows are fast like letters and the turtle is slow like the bureaucracy; Yuna laughs at the turtle. Light, dry humor.
deadpan, a dry joke, not smiling

In the cool, quiet archive, an archivist brings out 1970s maps of Gràcia. Yuna finds the vanished street, labeled in Castilian "C. del Relojero" rather than the Catalan "Rellotger"; Marc explains that street names were in Castilian back then. Yuna learns "hemos encontrado" (we have found). A 1978 directory lists "Relojería Puig" at number 7: the workshop of Marc's grandfather. Hushed, rising excitement, then quiet.
excited, her finger on the map

column1: Y ahora… una tienda de móviles.
Sí. La calle ya no existe.

column2: In the midday heat, Marc and Yuna sit on the shaded cathedral steps. Yuna finally asks whether Martí is still alive; he is not. Marc puts his grandfather's watch, still ticking, in her palm. Yuna thanks him "for today". Sad and tender, understated.
hesitant, careful, afraid of the answer
reading her Spanish diary entry, plain and steady
